configuration.title: Studium
configuration.repoRoot.description: Path to a prototype-build clone (development mode: lesson-mcp is launched from its sources through tsx). Optional for an installed VSIX: the embedded server dist/lesson-mcp.mjs is used when no clone is found.
configuration.bundlesRoot.description: Directory the lesson-mcp server resolves bundle_ref against (BUNDLES_ROOT). Leave empty to use the checkout's fixtures/ folder when the extension runs from a Studium checkout, else your personal library (~/.studium/library, or <STUDIUM_HOME>/library), where lessons an assistant builds for you land.
configuration.bundleRef.description: The bundle to open (relative to bundlesRoot). Defaults to the L1 atomistique demo.
configuration.communityBundlesRoot.descr: Root the 'Community contributions' command discovers approved learner-authored bundles against: the root of all courses, where scene-synth's decide_item path emits <root>/<course>/community/community-<item>.zip. Leave empty to reuse studium.bundlesRoot. The canonical course is never mutated; community items are additive.
configuration.assets.description: Where the webview loads KaTeX/Vega from: 'vendor' (offline, bundled in media/vendor, air-gap safe) or 'cdn' (jsdelivr).
configuration.assets.enum.0: Offline: KaTeX/Vega bundled in media/vendor (air-gap safe).
configuration.telemetryConsent.descripti: Opt in to consented, pseudonymized class telemetry (STUDIUM_TELEMETRY_CONSENT).
configuration.showGraph.description: Open a companion live Learning-Workflow-Graph panel that repaints each turn (typed-graph-lens).
configuration.graphView.description: Graph scope: 'student' (ego-graph around the current frontier) or 'teacher' (the whole graph).
configuration.showMastery.description: Show the live per-concept mastery bar in the lesson pane. OFF by default: it is a teacher/model signal, and showing it to a learner during a quiz can leak the answer (try options, watch which raises mastery). Turn on only for teacher demos.
configuration.modalityPreference.descrip: Modality-adaptive rendering (Ciussi, "comment mieux apprendre si je suis visuel"). Reorders and emphasizes each scene's artifacts toward the learner's preferred modality. Content-preserving: nothing is removed; the non-preferred modality is collapsed, never hidden.
configuration.modalityPreference.enum.0: Lead with the visual modality: 3D orbital / molecule / plot / spectrum renders are ordered first and expanded; equations & text are collapsed (kept, openable).
configuration.modalityPreference.enum.1: Lead with the textual modality: equations, markdown & concise summaries are ordered first and expanded; figures & 3D are collapsed (kept, openable).
configuration.modalityPreference.enum.2: Balanced: the authored order, no extra emphasis (default).
extension.description: Learn from adaptive lessons in VS Code and train your judgment of AI output: each scene is shown with its figures, equations and executed reference runs, and spaced reviews bring concepts back before you forget them.

viewsWelcome.empty:
No lesson found yet.
Ask your assistant to build one ("I want to learn something with Studium"): it appears in your personal library. Or choose a folder of lessons.
[Pick a course](command:studium.pickLesson)
[Get started](command:studium.openWalkthrough)
walkthrough.title: Get started with Studium
walkthrough.description: Learn from your own sources with your assistant, judge what an AI produces, and review before you forget.
walkthrough.step.open.title: Pick and open a lesson
walkthrough.step.open.description:
Open the Studium icon in the activity bar, pick a course from your lessons folder, then open it. The lesson pane shows each scene (figures, equations, plots) and asks you questions, one step at a time.
[Pick a course](command:studium.pickLesson)  ·  [Open the current course](command:studium.openLesson)
walkthrough.step.selfStudy.title: Learn a topic with your assistant
walkthrough.step.selfStudy.description:
Tell Codex or Claude Code "I want to learn X with Studium". It gathers sources and builds a lesson for you in your personal library. Open that lesson here: right-click its lesson.json and choose "Studium: Open this lesson", or follow the link your assistant gives you.
[Pick a course](command:studium.pickLesson)
walkthrough.step.judge.title: Judge the AI's output
walkthrough.step.judge.description: On a "spot the flaw" scene, a deck of claims asks you to flag the incorrect ones and leave the correct ones alone. This is the heart of Studium: calibrating your judgment of what an AI tells you.
walkthrough.step.run.title: Run a reproduction
walkthrough.step.run.description:
A reproduction scene runs a real capsule in your workspace. Studium shows you the exact command and asks you to confirm before anything starts, and never runs it itself.
[Run the reproduction](command:studium.runReproduction)
walkthrough.step.review.title: Review what you have learned
walkthrough.step.review.description:
Spaced review brings a concept back when you are about to forget it. The status bar shows how many are due ("Studium · 2 to review") and the Reviews entry in the sidebar lists them.
[Open the Studium sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.studium)
walkthrough.media.pane.alt: The Studium lesson pane: a scene with a figure, three answer choices and a continue button.
walkthrough.media.deck.alt: The verdict deck: three claims, one flagged as incorrect, and a submit button.
walkthrough.media.review.alt: The review screen: a ring of concepts due, the list of concepts to revisit and the days of the coming week.
